body:
"Hank" wrote:
> 
> John Preston wrote:
> >
> > I've been thinking that it would be lots of fun to print up
> > thousands of copies of the Manifesto in cheap miniature booklet
> > form and distribute them to junior high school students and
> > mental patients.
> >
> > Normally rebellious adolescent boys and mental patients should
> > latch right onto the sections that talk about being coerced to
> > study, brainwashing, being drugged, and behavior modification
> > to fit the needs of the system.
> >
> > =============================================================
> > "The system needs scientists, mathematicians and engineers.
> >  It can't function without them. So heavy pressure is put on
> >  children to excel in these fields."                   -- FC
> > =============================================================
> 
> An interesting choice of tag line.  "So heavy pressure is put on children to
> excel in these fields."  This is not society's fault - this is his parents'
> fault.  This is another example of the Unabomber blaming society for his own
> personal problems.
> 
> - "Hank"

You can't totally separate society from personal problems. During the 
'50's, "Science" was universally worshipped because we had to beat the 
Russians to the moon, and build bigger bombs (the Thermonuclear kind, not 
the kind in wooden boxes) with which to blow them Commies to hell.

Heavy pressure is STILL put on children to excel academically, so that 
they can incur huge student loan debts, compete with swarms of similarly 
pedigreed patricians (a college degree is a sign of being "a higher class 
person") for the few jobs available, and most likely be downsized/made 
obsolete within a few years, if they are not lucky enough to have majored 
in one of the "hot" fields. Or, if they can't make the grade 
academically, they can suffer from chronic low self-esteem and compete 
for the minimum wage jobs.
"But don't let's blame society for their personal shortcomings", 'cause 
society never does anything wrong.
--Shadow
